kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-14.title: Unfold by reflections
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-14.body:
The path has four straight pieces: $A\to BC\to AD\to BC\to D$. Each piece crosses the square from one of the sides $AD$, $BC$ to the other, so it has a "vertical" part of length 1; the horizontal parts (along $AD$) add up to $AD=1$ if the path always moves towards $D$.

Reflect the square across $BC$, then the copy across its far side, and so on: the zigzag becomes a path from $A$ to the image of $D$, which is $4$ units away vertically and $1$ unit horizontally. The shortest path is the straight segment:
$$\sqrt{4^2+1^2}=\sqrt{17}.$$
It touches $BC$ at horizontal positions $\frac14$ and $\frac34$ and $AD$ at $\frac12$.

**Answer: (E) $\sqrt{17}$**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-14.title: Cauchy–Schwarz
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-14.body:
If the horizontal parts of the four pieces are $h_1,\dots,h_4\ge0$ (we may assume no backtracking) with $h_1+\dots+h_4 = 1$, the length is $\sum\sqrt{1+h_i^2}$. By the Minkowski (triangle) inequality, $\sum\sqrt{1+h_i^2}\ge\sqrt{(1+1+1+1)^2+(\sum h_i)^2}=\sqrt{17}$, with equality when all $h_i=\frac14$.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-24.title: Use $R=\frac{abc}{4\,\text{Area}}$
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-24.body:
Let the side be 3, $M$ the midpoint of $BC$. The height is $AM=\frac{3\sqrt3}2$, and $K,L$ are at distance $\frac12$ from $M$. So $KL=1$ and $AK=AL=\sqrt{\frac14+\frac{27}4}=\sqrt7$.

Area of $AKL$ $=\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac{3\sqrt3}2=\frac{3\sqrt3}4$, so
$$R_{AKL}=\frac{\sqrt7\cdot\sqrt7\cdot1}{4\cdot\frac{3\sqrt3}4}=\frac7{3\sqrt3}.$$
For $ABC$: $R=\frac{3}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt3$. Ratio $\frac{7}{3\sqrt3}:\sqrt3 = 7:9$.

**Answer: (B) 7:9**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-24.title: Law of sines
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-24.body:
In triangle $AKL$ the angle at $K$ satisfies $\sin\angle AKL=\frac{AM}{AK}=\frac{3\sqrt3/2}{\sqrt7}$, and the opposite side is $AL=\sqrt7$. So $2R_{AKL}=\frac{AL}{\sin K}=\frac{7\cdot 2}{3\sqrt3}$. For $ABC$: $2R=\frac{3}{\sin60^\circ}=2\sqrt3$. Ratio $\frac{14/(3\sqrt3)}{2\sqrt3}=\frac79$.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-26.title: Rational root test
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-26.body:
All coefficients are positive, so any root is negative. An integer root $r$ divides the constant term $b$ (from $b = -r(ar+c)$), so $r=-1$ or $r=-b$.

- $r=-1$: $a-c+b=0$, i.e. $c=a+b$. If $a,b$ are both odd, $a+b$ is even and not prime; so $a=2$, $b=3$, $c=5$ — these are consecutive primes ✓ ($2x^2+5x+3=(2x+3)(x+1)$).
- $r=-b$: $ab^2-cb+b=0$, i.e. $c=ab+1$. For odd $a,b$ this is even; for $a=2,b=3$ it gives $7\ne5$.

So $b=3$ is the only possibility: **1** value.

**Answer: (A) 1**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-29.title: Count by the outer pair
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-29.body:
There are $\binom{10}3=120$ equally likely choices. One number is the average of the other two exactly when the three form an arithmetic progression $x<m<z$. Such a triple is determined by the outer pair $x,z$, which must have the same parity (so that $m=\frac{x+z}2$ is an integer). Pairs of same parity: $\binom52+\binom52=20$.

Probability $\frac{20}{120}=\frac16$.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-29.title: Count by the middle
kangaroo-ca-2019-g1112-29.body:
Middle number $m$ with common difference $d\ge1$: need $m-d\ge1$ and $m+d\le10$, so $d\le\min(m-1,10-m)$. For $m=2,\dots,9$: $1,2,3,4,4,3,2,1$ — total 20. Probability $\frac{20}{120}=\frac16$.

**Answer: (B)**
